events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.33 (model confidence 0.85)
events.body:
RydeTAXI is metered, so extra distance enters the fare directly and is refundable under RD-2; the GPS record shows a single off-route segment 21:57–22:04 driving 4.13 km where the optimal route covers 1.77 km, i.e. +2.36 km [F3], against an overall +2.6 km over 16.5 km [F1][F2]. That segment is an unexcused deviation unless RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 excuses it [RD-1][RD-2].

RD-4 fails: the accident record is an LTA incident lying 0 m from the optimal route, but it was reported at 22:07, after the segment began at 21:57, so it was not "reported before the detour" and cannot exempt it; the AYE and CTE speed-band facts are band 4 only and, on RD-4(b), a speed band alone does not exempt [F3][F10][F11][F12][RD-4]. The driver's statement that he "went round" an accident is a post-trip assertion of reasonable cause, and RD-4 requires traffic-fact corroboration for the replaced stretch; this incident fails the timing test. It remains relevant only as evidence that the driver chose the route himself, not at the rider's request [F9][RD-4].

RD-3 does not apply: the trace records no stop in the segment, so no rider-named place could have been stopped at; and with no rider request of any kind the driver's choice cannot be excused under RD-3(b) [F3][F8][RD-3].

RD-5 fails at its threshold: the only agreement on record is the driver's post-trip statement, which is a claim, not rider consent (G11), and the complete chat record contains no rider message at all before 21:57:35 — so there is nothing the rider agreed to, and no scope to read. This is a driver-chosen route change with no rider consent, which counts in full [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

The refund follows the trace formula using this trip's own rate, the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km: $26.93 ÷ 19.10 km = $1.4099/km (unrounded); 2.36 km × $1.4099/km = $3.3274, i.e. $3.33 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The remaining difference between the billed excess (2.57 km = $3.62 [F4]) and the segment sum is not refunded, as RD-2 excludes mileage outside the identified segments. The waiting fee of $0.02 is a metered waiting unit (0.1 min × $0.26/min) and stays charged under RD-3(c) [F5][RD-3]. FARE-1 / FARE-2 add nothing: the fare consists only of published components and the dataset carries no toll field [F7][FARE-1][FARE-2].

Account action is not triggered: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, and the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (the two upheld disputes are no-show, not route), so no flag_account [F15][RD-6]. The rider's own profile (rating 4.9, 0 upheld disputes) does not affect the outcome [F14].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the (empty) chat and the driver's statement in full; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no escalation under SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 [F8][F9][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the measured segment, the complete chat record and the fare breakdown settle every element this ruling needs [F3][F7][F8].

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 21:57:35 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F9: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “There was an accident on Ayer Rajah Expressway; I went round it. The extra distance was unavoidable.” (F9)
